ig_carousel_topic.topic: The Kelly criterion explained without the math degree
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you bet on each game?
Most bettors guess. Kelly has an answer.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: The common mistake: flat-betting everything the same, or going big when you feel confident. Neither approach accounts for your actual edge on a given play.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Kelly says your bet size should scale with your edge. Bigger edge, more on the line. Smaller edge, less. The formula keeps you from blowing up on a bad run.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Example: You have a 55% win rate on a -110 line. Full Kelly says bet about 5.5% of your bankroll. Most sharp bettors use half-Kelly (2.75%) to absorb variance without the swings.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: You don't need to run the formula every night. Knowing the logic changes how you size bets. That alone puts you ahead of most casual players.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Kelly criterion in plain terms. Size your bets to your edge, not your gut. This one concept separates disciplined bettors from the rest.
